items.item: Batch encrypt + decrypt for app on/de-boarding: Tier 1 endpoints
items.notes: POST /encrypt/batch and POST /decrypt/batch both implemented -- multiple items per call, correlated back by a caller-supplied key, always 200 with per-item success/error status. Both reuse the existing single-item encrypt()/decrypt() methods unmodified per item, sequential not concurrent (pending real HSM throughput numbers), share hsm.service.batch-max-items (default 100). Decrypt-batch's token-or-legacy-fields check is a per-item runtime outcome (inside decrypt()), not a whole-batch Bean Validation rejection like encrypt's plaintext checks -- one malformed item doesn't sink the batch. 15 tests total (7 encrypt + 8 decrypt), full suite 55/55. See java/docs/BULK_OPERATIONS.md. Not built: audit duration_ms/time-taken (only counts + a single completion timestamp exist today).

items.item: Add duration_ms (time taken) to batch_encrypt/batch_decrypt audit events
items.notes: Both audit events currently carry item/success/failure counts and the standard single completion timestamp every audit event gets -- no start time or duration field, so elapsed time can't be derived from the audit trail today. Small: capture Instant.now() at the top of encryptBatch/decryptBatch, compute elapsed millis before the existing audit call, add one field to each. Documented in java/docs/BULK_OPERATIONS.md.

items.item: Publish client-side bulk/chunking reference guidance (not a service)
items.notes: Corrected from an earlier design: bulk/file-chunking is NOT a service this repo builds -- reaching into an app's own DB/blob storage would need a new cross-app storage grant, and bulk crypto-shred already needs zero new capability (deleting ciphertext_token is already effective shredding per DEMO.md Sec6). Instead: document the chunk-per-DEK + manifest + stitch-back pattern for app teams driving their own bulk jobs against the Tier 1 batch endpoint, and consider publishing a thin reference client library. See java/docs/BULK_OPERATIONS.md.

items.item: Tier 3 (proposed): local envelope encryption via a separate hsm-bulk-service + CLNT library
items.notes: Design proposal only, not built, not reviewed -- needs security/crypto sign-off first (Phase 0 of the development plan). App-side CLNT does local AES-256-GCM using DEKs issued by a new, separately deployable hsm-bulk-service (POST /dek/issue, POST /dek/unwrap; new dek_issue/dek_unwrap scopes), each DEK still individually KEK-wrapped and persisted via the HSM exactly as today -- DEK-per-record is preserved, not traded away for throughput. Motivation is reducing SVC's own compute/bandwidth footprint as a shared multi-tenant resource during large onboarding/de-boarding migrations, not reducing HSM RPS (which stays unchanged either way). Scoped strictly to onboarding/de-boarding bookend events, not steady-state traffic -- apps go back to single/Tier-1-batch afterward. See java/docs/BULK_OPERATIONS.md "Tier 3" and "Development plan" sections.

items.item: Distroless/minimal runtime base image
items.notes: eclipse-temurin:21-jre-jammy (full Ubuntu userland) replaced with gcr.io/distroless/java21-debian13:nonroot -- Debian-based, ships Temurin OpenJDK 21 preinstalled, no shell/package manager. Fixed uid/gid 65532 (the distroless nonroot convention) replaces the old groupadd/useradd 'hsmsvc' (1001) user; helm/hsm-core-service/values.yaml securityContext updated to match. Motivated by a real environment issue, not just staleness: behind a corporate firewall, apt-get needed a JFrog-mirrored Ubuntu archive with credentials configured before it could even reach the Jammy repos -- distroless removes apt-get from this Dockerfile entirely, so there's no apt/deb mirror to configure at all anymore.

Trust store password also moved from a hardcoded 'changeit' literal to corporateCa.trustStorePassword (still defaults to 'changeit' -- cacerts holds only public certs, so this only guards integrity, not confidentiality -- but no longer a literal string a secret-scanner flags).

items.item: hsm-bulk-service (SVC) -- POST /dek/issue + POST /dek/unwrap
items.notes: See java/docs/TIER3_POC_BUILD.md and java/docs/BULK_OPERATIONS.md's Tier 3 section. New module (V6 migration adds app_registrations.public_key_pem), scoped to Phases 1+2 -- admin key-provisioning endpoint (Phase 3) still deferred. Live BulkVsBatchBenchmark (200 records, both services local/mocked): Batch 304 items/sec vs Bulk 145.7 items/sec -- Bulk was slower here, likely RSA-2048 OAEP unwrap overhead per item on the CLNT side; doesn't contradict Tier 3's actual motivation (SVC shared-process footprint under concurrent load, not single-caller throughput), but is a real cost a production pilot needs to size.

items.item: hsm-bulk-client (CLNT) -- standalone Bulk DB + Bulk File client
items.notes: New module, genuinely separate from SVC (not merged) -- calls POST /dek/issue|unwrap over HTTP, does all AES-GCM locally, no server-side machinery of its own (no auth filter, no JPA). BULK DB: config-driven source/target table+column mapping, independently addressable JDBC URL/schema/table per side, one DEK per column value (not per row), keyset-paginated reads. BULK File: source/target each independently local disk or ADLS (FileStore interface -- mixed pairs like ADLS-to-disk fall out for free), one DEK per whole file, chunks stitched via length-prefixed binary framing (not newline-delimited -- ciphertext can contain a literal 0x0A). Verified live end-to-end against real hsm-core-service + hsm-bulk-service: BULK DB and BULK File round trips both byte-for-byte identical, including a spot-check through hsm-core-service's real /decrypt and a multi-chunk (8-chunk) binary file. Answers BULK_OPERATIONS.md's open 'reference client library' question -- this is that client, not a separate future item.

items.item: hsm-bulk-service Docker/Helm deployment
items.notes: java/docker/Dockerfile.hsm-bulk-service (same distroless multi-stage pattern as hsm-core-service) + full helm/hsm-bulk-service/ chart (Deployment, Service, ConfigMap, Secret, ServiceAccount/Workload Identity, HPA, PDB, NetworkPolicy, corporate-CA initContainer). Two deliberate differences from hsm-core-service's chart: replicaCount 1 + PDB off by default (scoped bulk-window service, not always-on traffic -- a minAvailable:1 PDB on one replica blocks voluntary node drains), and probes.type: tcp by default (no health endpoint on SVC yet). Adding the two new modules to the parent POM's <modules> broke the EXISTING Dockerfile.hsm-core-service/Dockerfile.cek-rotation builds (Maven's reactor needs every module's pom.xml present even with -pl/-am) -- both fixed. hsm-bulk-client stays a plain runnable jar, no Docker/K8s for it -- scripts/build.sh + scripts/run.sh + config-examples/ instead. Validated via helm lint/template (no Docker daemon or K8s cluster in this environment to validate a real build/deploy).

items.item: hsm-core-service: stop embedding DB credentials in DATABASE_URL
items.notes: hsm-core-service previously expected credentials embedded directly in DATABASE_URL (postgresql://user:pass@host/db) -- but Hikari and Hibernate both print the JDBC URL at startup unconditionally ('Database JDBC URL [...]', 'HikariPool-1 - Added connection ... url=...'), which ships to Splunk via this service's own log pipeline; an embedded password would land in plaintext in every pod's logs. Fixed by adding separate DATABASE_USERNAME/DATABASE_PASSWORD properties (matching hsm-bulk-service's and application-demo.yml's existing pattern), updated helm/hsm-core-service's Secret template accordingly. Verified: hsm-core-service still starts and passes its health check with the new fields; 55/55 tests still pass.

items.item: DEK naming/reuse -- dek_name on /encrypt, /encrypt/batch, /dek/issue
items.notes: Optional dek_name lets a caller reuse the current DEK for (app_id, dek_name) instead of minting one per call -- opt-in, default behavior unchanged. V7 migration adds edek_records.dek_name (permanent) + current_dek_name (nulled on rotation, uniquely indexed per app_id via a shadow-column pair since H2 rejects Postgres's partial-unique-index syntax). Mirrored in EncryptionService.resolveDek (primes DekCache on reuse) and DekIssueService.issueOne (no DekCache there, still one HSM unwrap per reuse but far fewer DEKs minted). Fingerprint left null on named rows -- one edek_id gets many iv/tag pairs under reuse; the existing null-gated check needed no changes. Classification bound per-name: explicit conflict rejects (422), blank-value backfills, blank-blank is a no-op. Fixed a bug: dek_name sent as '' broke the unique index on the next unnamed call -- normalized blank-to-null in both DTOs. Reverses BULK_OPERATIONS.md's 'DEK-per-record, non-negotiable' rejection as a narrow, opt-in exception. 59/59 + 9/9 tests pass.

items.item: Named-DEK rotation scheduler (age-based, hsm-core-service)
items.notes: NamedDekRotationScheduler mirrors KekRotationScheduler's shape (@PostConstruct + CronTrigger, demo-mode guard). RotationService.rotateNamedDeks(maxAgeHours) sweeps current-status edek_records rows with a non-null current_dek_name older than the threshold (default 720h/30d, hsm.named-dek-rotation.*), mints a fresh DEK per row, retires the old one (rotated, current_dek_name cleared, dek_name kept for history). Deliberately time-based, not usage-count-based -- hsm-core-service has no visibility into how many values a caller encrypts with a DEK it hands out (that happens client-side), so a lookup counter could never be trustworthy. One real gotcha: the old row's UPDATE must be saveAndFlush'd before the new row's INSERT, since Hibernate's default flush order is by operation type (inserts before updates), not registration order -- inserting first would transiently violate the unique index within the same transaction. Verified via a dedicated integration test exercising a full rotation round trip.

items.item: hsm-bulk-client: Azure AD Workload Identity auth for long-running jobs
items.notes: Previously SvcClient sent a single static config token for a whole job run -- fine for demo mode's never-expiring fixed strings, but a real Azure AD JWT (~1h TTL) would expire mid-run on any job longer than that. New TokenProvider abstraction: StaticTokenProvider (today's behavior, default svc.auth-mode: STATIC) or AzureAdTokenProvider (svc.auth-mode: AZURE_AD), which calls TokenCredential.getToken() fresh before every request -- a cache hit on nearly every call since the Azure Identity SDK caches internally and only re-acquires near expiry, so no manual TTL tracking needed. Same Workload Identity -> Managed Identity -> DefaultAzureCredential cascade already used by AzureKeyVaultKekClient and AdlsFileStore, kept as its own copy per this repo's no-shared-library convention. No client secret anywhere in the chain.

items.item: hsm-bulk-client: DbBulkJob named-DEK batching + unwrap dedup
items.notes: ClientProperties.Db.ColumnMapping gained dekName -- DbBulkJob.encrypt() resolves a named column's DEK once for the whole job run (issueNamedColumnDeks(), before the pagination loop starts), not per row or per sub-batch. decrypt() separately dedups by edek_id (not the existing per-row correlation key) before both the /dek/unwrap call and the local RSA-OAEP unwrap -- the RSA step, not the HTTP round trip, was the dominant cost in the original bulk-vs-batch benchmark, so deduping only the network call would have missed the larger win.

items.item: app_decrypt_grants: per-dek_name grant scoping
items.notes: app_decrypt_grants is app-to-app only ((grantee_app_id, owner_app_id), no column/name scoping) -- this predates dek_name and was already this coarse for ordinary DEK-per-record data, so it's not a new gap in kind. But dek_name now gives the system a real taxonomy (customers.ssn vs. customers.account_number) that grant scoping could use but doesn't -- an auditor could reasonably ask why access control doesn't distinguish what DEK issuance already does. Natural fix: extend AppDecryptGrant's key with an optional, nullable dek_name (NULL = today's blanket grant, unchanged; a value scopes to just that name). Not required to ship dek_name reuse itself -- tracked separately.

items.item: hsm-bulk-client: DbBulkJob connection pooling, batch-insert fix, and parallelism
items.notes: Prompted by a real report: a 2M-row, 4-column db encrypt job took 4 hours. Root causes, diagnosed against the actual reported config, not guesswork: DriverManagerDataSource (unpooled -- every JDBC op pays full connection-setup cost) and subChunkByItemCap capping insert batches to dek-batch-max-items even when no /dek/issue HTTP call remained to cap. Fixed: HikariDataSource (pool sized to parallelism+2), reWriteBatchedInserts=true auto-appended to Postgres URLs, subChunkByItemCap returns the whole page as one chunk when columnsPerRow=0. New client.db.parallelism (default 1, unchanged): partitions the key range via a bounded, one-time set of OFFSET boundary lookups (not per-page OFFSET, which this design still avoids), one worker per partition. Verified against real Postgres: 9,973-row table split into 4 partitions (2494/2493/2493/2493), every id seen exactly once under real concurrent access.

items.item: hsm-bulk-client: DbBulkJob checkpoint/resume
items.notes: New client.db.checkpoint (enabled/resume/job-id/table-name, default disabled -- zero overhead unless opted in). A batch's data insert and its checkpoint update commit in one transaction (TransactionTemplate/DataSourceTransactionManager), so a resumed run can never skip un-written rows nor re-process written ones. Deliberately not built on an ON CONFLICT upsert against the actual target table -- the checkpoint table owns its own guaranteed-unique job_id key, so resume works without requiring the source/target key to be provably unique. Under parallelism>1 each partition gets its own derived checkpoint (job-id-p0, p1...). Verified against real Postgres, 12 checks including a simulated mid-transaction crash: confirmed neither the data row nor the checkpoint landed; a real commit landed both; a second batch upserted (not duplicated) the checkpoint row.

items.item: hsm-bulk-service: Named-DEK rotation scheduler
items.notes: Closes a real, previously-unflagged gap: DEKs issued via POST /dek/issue with a name (DbBulkJob's per-column dek-name, and the new File-job dek-name below) had no rotation at all -- unlike hsm-core-service's own /encrypt dek_name path. New NamedDekRotationScheduler/RotationService, mirroring hsm-core-service's exactly (hsm.named-dek-rotation.*, same age-based reasoning, same saveAndFlush-before-save Hibernate flush-order fix). Verified booting the real Spring app against real Postgres, 13 checks: old row retires (rotated, current_dek_name cleared, wrapped form untouched and still decryptable), a fresh row takes over reuse under the same name, and -- importantly -- a freshly-rotated-in row is NOT re-swept under a realistic 24h cutoff, confirming the age-based logic actually discriminates, not just that the sweep runs.

items.item: hsm-bulk-client: FileBulkJob dek-name, parallelism, checkpoint/resume, and decrypt dedup fix
items.notes: client.file.dek-name mirrors DbBulkJob's dek-name but scoped to the whole job (one business purpose, e.g. all-customer-files), not a column -- and persists across every future run, which is why the rotation scheduler above had to exist first. client.file.parallelism splits the file list into even groups (files are independent/unordered, no boundary-key math needed). client.file.checkpoint uses a single batched manifest file in the target store (no per-file marker -- doubles ADLS operation cost; no new DB dependency); flush-interval (default 1000) decoupled from files-per-batch after measuring the coupling cost directly (58s to 10.9s on 60k files, 6000 to 60 rewrites). Found and fixed while verifying: decrypt wasn't deduping by edek_id like DbBulkJob's decrypt does. Verified with a genuine kill -9 mid-run on 60,000 real files: resumed to exactly 60,000/60,000 files/manifest entries, zero duplicates; dek_issued showed 1 event not 60,000; decrypted output byte-for-byte identical to source.

items.item: Tier 3 security/crypto review -- now spans two shared-DEK surfaces, not one
items.notes: Already-open item (see BULK_OPERATIONS.md Open Decisions) made more pressing by this round: dek-name now also exists on the File job, scoped to a whole job/business purpose rather than a single DB column -- a coarser, larger blast radius per name than the DB case (one column is one kind of data; one file job can span many kinds of content under one source tree). Real code exists and is verified working end-to-end for both surfaces; the dedicated security/crypto review this doc has called for since before any of Tier 3 was built has still not happened.
